description:
Follow-up to bd:JMAP-6r7c.57: the trust-scope fix to CustomCaTransport (replace bundled webpki-roots with the private CA only) should have a defense-in-depth integration test that proves the behavior.

Apparatus:

- rcgen 0.13+ to generate test certificates at runtime.
- Two test TLS servers (axum + axum-server with rustls):
  1. Server A: certificate signed by a 'fake public CA' that we then install into webpki-roots-like position OR a wiremock-rustls setup that presents a webpki-rooted cert.
  2. Server B: certificate signed by a private CA we generate and pass to CustomCaTransport.
- Assertions:
  - JmapClient with CustomCaTransport(server B's CA) connecting to server B succeeds.
  - JmapClient with CustomCaTransport(server B's CA) connecting to server A fails with TLS handshake error surfacing as ClientError::Http(HttpError) whose source chain contains a CertificateUnknown / UnknownIssuer rustls error.

The test stays under tests/, uses rcgen as a dev-dep (no production-runtime dep), and runs offline.

Out of scope for the bug fix bead because spinning up real-rustls test servers is a meaningful infrastructure addition (the workspace currently uses wiremock 0.6 which does NOT speak TLS — wiremock has an https feature on a fork but is not in the current Cargo.lock).

Alternative if the rustls-server apparatus is too heavy: a unit-style assertion that reads the reqwest::ClientBuilder configuration the function generates (without actually making a request), checking the tls_built_in_root_certs flag. reqwest's ClientBuilder is mostly opaque, so this may require a thin wrapper that the test can inspect.
title: test: rcgen-based integration test for CustomCaTransport trust scope
